hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Run the permutation's dependence audit on those 9 atoms before anything else. If the target order violates a def-use edge legal in OUR colouring, claim.law.C1_permute-recolor-composition-needs-a-permutation-legal-in-our-colouring.20260901.v1 kills the whole route in zero builds. The specific edge to check is the one the two streams disagree about: the target gives the gSysFlags value and the gPadStartHoldTimer HA half the SAME register across a live range boundary -- `@0x41c lwz r3,0(0) @gSysFlags(EMB_SDA21)` is consumed at `@0x42c rlwinm r0,r3,0,20,18` and only then is r3 redefined by `@0x430 lis r3,0 @gPadStartHoldTimer(ADDR16_HA)` -- whereas ours keeps those two values in separate registers (`@0x41c lwz r4` and `@0x424 lis r3`). A permutation that moves our `@0x424 lis r3,0` down past our `@0x42c rlwinm r0,r4,...` is legal only if that r3/r4 split is preserved, so the audit must decide whether the recolor stage is required BEFORE the permutation rather than after it.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- the atom list, both orders, and every instruction quoted above were read off the aligned `fnasm --diff` view of 0x400:0x460 and are target-accurate, but the dependence audit itself was NOT run and no webfrank stage was configured or tried. `webfrank_audit.py --grep sysResetService` returns 0 candidates, which per claim.law.RQ_webfrank-audit-silence-is-not-ineligibility.20260901.v1 is silence, not a verdict.
hypothesis.statement: The window is a composed webfrank instruction_permutation + register_fields customer, not a source customer. The permutation is 9 atoms over [0x41c,0x440), quoted from `fnasm.py game/sys/sysservice.c sysResetService 0x400:0x460 --diff`. OUR order and defining instructions: `@0x41c lwz r4,0(0) @gSysFlags(EMB_SDA21)`, `@0x420 li r0,4`, `@0x424 lis r3,0 @gPadStartHoldTimer(ADDR16_HA)`, `@0x428 mtctr r0`, `@0x42c rlwinm r0,r4,0,20,18`, `@0x430 stw r0,0(0) @gSysFlags(EMB_SDA21)`, `@0x434 addi r4,r3,0 @gPadStartHoldTimer(ADDR16_LO)`, `@0x438 lwz r5,0(0) @gPadCur(EMB_SDA21)`, `@0x43c li r3,0`. THE TARGET's order and defining instructions: `@0x41c lwz r3,0(0) @gSysFlags(EMB_SDA21)`, `@0x420 li r0,4`, `@0x424 mtctr r0`, `@0x428 lwz r5,0(0) @gPadCur(EMB_SDA21)`, `@0x42c rlwinm r0,r3,0,20,18`, `@0x430 lis r3,0 @gPadStartHoldTimer(ADDR16_HA)`, `@0x434 stw r0,0(0) @gSysFlags(EMB_SDA21)`, `@0x438 li r6,0`, `@0x43c addi r4,r3,0 @gPadStartHoldTimer(ADDR16_LO)`. So the recolor stage is two rows: the gSysFlags value, defined `@0x41c lwz r4,...` in ours against `@0x41c lwz r3,...` in target, and the byte-offset induction, defined `@0x43c li r3,0` in ours against `@0x438 li r6,0` in target (its consumer is `@0x44c add r6,r4,r3` in ours against `@0x44c add r3,r4,r6` in target). The address base r4 is defined by an addi from the HA half in BOTH streams and needs no recolor. Provenance for the source-exhaustion bar is now complete: v2 capped declaration order and address spelling, this record caps statement order and condition spelling, and no probe has ever moved the window.
